Thanks again for taking the demo this morning — good discussion. Quick recap and recommended next steps based on what you shared: 

- Deployment preference: you mentioned a strong preference for a cloud-hosted evaluation (fast onboarding) but legal wants clarity on network residency and DPA.
- Primary workload: user-facing summarization + routing to internal KB (short prompts, avg. 120 tokens output).
- Scale expectation for pilot: ~100k requests/day (peak ~60 reqs/s), mostly daytime US traffic.

Recommended path (short): Start with a Hosted API sandbox trial so you can validate latency and integration quickly. If resource or compliance needs change, we can map to Dedicated or Private later (we do smooth porting).

Next steps I propose: 
1) We provision a sandbox org and two endpoints (/v1/chat, /v1/embeddings) for PayFlux (no infra commitment).
2) Monica will share a short ops checklist (IP allowlist, sample payloads, SLI targets).
3) Legal: we’ll surface the DPA + data residency notes — hosted evaluation keeps data encrypted at rest in our US region; can discuss Private/VPC if audit requires on-prem or customer-managed keys.

Attachments: payflux-demo-deck.pdf, network-schematic.png (demo slides + your topology notes).

Would you like us to spin up sandbox access tomorrow? If so, please confirm an IP allowlist range (or we can do token-based access first).

Thanks,

Appreciate the quick reply — answers inline and a short ops checklist attached (hosted_quickstart_checklist.pdf). Summary below: 

- Logs/audit: Sandbox provides request/response traces and an activity audit log view in Console (searchable). Data retention is configurable per org; for sandbox we default to 7 days but can extend for legal review. We do not surface full PII unless included in payloads; recommend safe-scrubbing during early tests.

- Sandbox rate limits (default):
  • 60 requests/sec aggregate per sandbox org (burst to 90 for short periods)
  • 400k tokens/minute overall
  • Per-endpoint concurrency: recommend limiting to 20 concurrent requests for chat-style endpoints during integration (we can raise if needed).

- Best practices for your workload: short prompts + KV/prefix caching is ideal. If you use our prefix KV cache you can reduce token usage by ~15–30% for repeated context. We’ll enable caching on the /v1/chat sandbox endpoint.

- Network & security: Hosted evaluation will run in our US region (us-west-2). We support IP allowlist, API tokens, and syslog export for audit streams. If PayFlux requires customer-managed keys or on-prem data residency, that’s when we recommend Private/VPC — but that’s a migration after you validate integration.

Next actions I’ll take today:
1) Provision sandbox (payflux-pilot-0182) and share credentials + Console link: https://app.redwood.ai/sandbox/payflux-pf-0182
2) Toggle KV prefix cache on chat endpoint.
3) Share the hosted_quickstart_checklist.pdf (attached) with the minimal ops items — Monica will follow up for scheduling an ops call.

If that sounds good, confirm an IP/CIDR for allowlist and we’ll provision token access.

Best,
Ben
